title: Spiking Neural Processor T1 by Innatera
summary: The Spiking Neural Processor (SNP) T1 is a neuromorphic microcontroller SoC from Dutch company Innatera. Designed for battery-powered IoT and edge devices, it integrates spiking neural network (SNN), convolutional neural network (CNN), and CPU accelerators on a single chip with sub-milliwatt power consumption. The device features mixed-signal cores configurable into parallel neural topologies to process binary spike events alongside standard workloads via a 32-bit RISCV core. It supports diverse sensor interfaces including QSPI, I2C, UART, GPIO, and an integrated front-end ADC for analog inputs like physiological sensors or microphones. Innatera provides the Talamo SDK based on PyTorch to facilitate model training without specialized neuromorphic expertise.
tldr: Innatera's SNP T1 is a low-power SoC integrating SNN/CNN accelerators and CPU for real-time sensing in battery-constrained IoT devices, supported by an open-source software stack.
evidence: The Spiking Neural Processor (SNP) T1 is a neuromorphic chip produced by Innatera, a semiconductor company based in Delft, Netherlands.
- Power consumption in sub-mW or mW range
It integrates a spiking neural network accelerator, a convolutional neural network accelerator and a RISCV core.
